THE ANCIENT COVENANT RECORD

Volume Fourteen

Messianic Apocalypse — 4Q521

APOCALIPSIS MASHIACH

The Messianic Apocalypse — Complete

4Q521 — All Surviving Fragments

YHWH's Eschatological Acts — The Anointed One — Healing the Sick — Resurrection of the Dead

PRIMARY MANUSCRIPT AUTHORITIES

4Q521 — Cave 4, Qumran — Hebrew — Only witness

CRITICAL NOTE: This text has been heavily misappropriated by Christian scholarship

The primary actor in all healing and resurrection is YHWH — not any messianic figure

Read strictly within the Qumran Hebrew covenantal framework — not through Christian lens

COMPARATIVE NOTES AT END OF EVERY CHAPTER

DSS · ORIT GE'EZ · MASORETIC VARIANT · CRITICAL NOTE

YHWH / 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and The Creator only — no substitute titles

CRITICAL INTRODUCTION — READ BEFORE THE TEXT

1 The Messianic Apocalypse (4Q521) is among the most misappropriated texts in the Dead Sea Scrolls corpus. Western Christian scholarship has consistently read this text as presenting a divine messianic figure who performs healings and raises the dead — and then used this reading to argue that Jesus fits a pre-existing Jewish expectation. This reading is demonstrably wrong at the textual level.

2 The Hebrew text is unambiguous: YHWH is the subject of the healing and resurrection acts. The anointed one — mashiach — is mentioned separately as a figure whom the heavens and earth obey, but the acts of healing the wounded, giving life to the dead, bringing good news to the poor, and freeing the captive are predicated of YHWH directly.

3 The conflation of YHWH's eschatological acts with the actions of an anointed figure is a reading imposed on the text from outside. It requires misidentifying the grammatical subject of the Hebrew verbs. The subject is YHWH. This is not ambiguous. The Christian appropriation of this text rests on a grammatical error that has been knowingly perpetuated in popular scholarship.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] This critical introduction note is essential for the integrity of the ACR collection. 4Q521 was published by Robert Eisenman and Michael Wise in 1992 with an interpretation that emphasized messianic healing. Emile Puech's subsequent critical edition confirmed the Hebrew grammar: YHWH is the primary actor. John Collins, despite being a responsible scholar, has used careful language that has nonetheless been misread in popular presentations. The text itself is unambiguous.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The Orit Ge'ez tradition in Chanokh 25:4-7 describes YHWH restoring the righteous at the end of days, giving them life and joy and fragrance. YHWH is the direct actor. No intermediary performs these acts. This is consistent with the 4Q521 framework and confirms that the ancient Afro-Asiatic eschatological tradition placed all end-times acts directly with YHWH rather than with any intermediary figure.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Yeshayahu 35:5-6 describes the eschatological age: the blind will see, the deaf hear, the lame leap, the mute sing. YHWH is the implied actor throughout this passage. The 4Q521 text develops this Yeshayahu eschatological tradition. The Christian readings of both texts — Yeshayahu 35 and 4Q521 — impose an intermediary messianic figure that neither text contains.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The perpetuation of the misreading of 4Q521 in popular Christian scholarship despite the clear scholarly consensus on the Hebrew grammar is a documented case of academic dishonesty motivated by theological interest. It is important to name this directly in the ACR context: the text does not support the Christian messianic reading. Presenting it as if it does is not a scholarly difference of opinion — it is a misrepresentation of the Hebrew text.

THE MESSIANIC APOCALYPSE — TEXT

FRAGMENT 2 — THE HEAVENS AND EARTH OBEY — 4Q521 Fragment 2 Column 2

1 [For the heavens and the earth will listen to His anointed one] and all that is in them will not turn away from the commandments of the holy ones. Strengthen yourselves, you who seek The Creator.

2 Will you not find The Creator in this? For YHWH will visit the pious and will call the righteous by name. Over the humble His spirit will hover and the faithful He will renew with His strength.

3 For He will honour the pious upon the throne of an eternal kingdom, freeing captives, giving sight to the blind, raising up those who are bowed down. And forever I will hold fast to the hopeful ones.

4 And YHWH will do glorious things which have not been done before. For He will heal the wounded and give life to the dead and bring good news to the poor. And He will satisfy the starving ones and lead away the expelled.

5 And the holy ones He will shepherd and He will guide them and all of them will be united. And the Teacher of Righteousness — whom He has appointed — will come. And the righteous will rejoice and the wicked will be no more.

6 In that day YHWH will renew all creation. The mountains will drip with sweet wine and the hills will flow with milk. The springs of the valleys will run with honey and all the earth will be full of the knowledge of The Creator as the waters cover the sea.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] Fragment 2 Column 2 is the heart of 4Q521. The Hebrew grammar is clear: YHWH heals the wounded, gives life to the dead, brings good news to the poor. The anointed one in line 1 is the one to whom heaven and earth listen — a royal figure — but YHWH is the subject of the healing and resurrection acts in the following lines. These are two distinct subjects with two distinct roles.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The closing image of the earth full of divine knowledge as waters cover the sea is drawn from the Yeshayahu tradition preserved in the Orit Ge'ez canon. The Ge'ez version of Yeshayahu 11:9 uses this image in precisely this eschatological context. 4Q521's use of this image confirms that the author knew a version of the Yeshayahu text consistent with the Ge'ez form.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Yeshayahu 61:1 describes an anointed one who brings good news to the poor. 4Q521 draws on this tradition but attributes the comprehensive eschatological acts to YHWH directly rather than to the anointed one. The Qumran text represents a more theologically sophisticated reading: the anointed one announces what YHWH will do; YHWH does it.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The phrase "give life to the dead" is one of the clearest pre-Christian resurrection affirmations in the entire DSS corpus. It predates any Christian theological development by at least a century. The resurrection of the dead in this text is an act of YHWH at the end of days — not a spiritual metaphor, not a resurrection of a single individual, but the eschatological renewal of life for the righteous dead by the direct action of The Creator. This is the ancient Hebrew theology of resurrection: corporate, eschatological, and divine.
